dish.title: San Francisco Cioppino with Clams, Mussels, Shrimp, and Cod
dish.description: A tomato and white wine broth built on onion, fennel, garlic, red pepper flakes, and tomato paste with crushed tomatoes, clam juice, bay, and oregano, in which littleneck clams, mussels, shrimp, and chunks of cod are cooked just until done, finished with parsley and served with toasted sourdough.

recipe_version.title: San Francisco Cioppino with Clams, Mussels, Shrimp, and Cod
recipe_version.description: A tomato and white wine broth built on onion, fennel, garlic, red pepper flakes, and tomato paste with crushed tomatoes, clam juice, bay, and oregano, in which littleneck clams, mussels, shrimp, and chunks of cod are cooked just until done, finished with parsley and served with toasted sourdough.

ingredients.name: sourdough bread
ingredients.display_name: sourdough whose label lists wheat flour, water, salt, and culture

steps.title: Prep
steps.body: Scrub the clams and mussels, debearding the mussels and discarding any with cracked shells or that stay open when tapped. Chop the onion, slice the fennel and garlic, cut the cod, and chop the parsley.

steps.title: Build the base
steps.body: Heat 3 tbsp oil in the 6-quart Dutch oven over medium, about 1 minute. Cook the onion and fennel until soft, about 7 minutes, then the garlic, pepper flakes, and tomato paste for 2 minutes. Add the wine and simmer 2 minutes.

steps.title: Simmer the broth
steps.body: Add the crushed tomatoes, clam juice, 2 cups water, bay leaves, oregano, and salt. Bring to a simmer, about 5 minutes to come to a simmer, then simmer uncovered 15 minutes.

steps.title: Toast the bread
steps.body: While the broth simmers (overlap stated): brush the bread with 1 tbsp oil and toast it in the 12-inch skillet over medium, 4 slices at a time, about 2 minutes per side.

steps.title: Cook the seafood
steps.body: Add the clams, cover, and cook 4 minutes. Add the mussels and cod, cover, and cook 3 minutes. Add the shrimp, cover, and cook until the shellfish open, the shrimp are pink, and the cod reads 145 F, about 3 minutes. Discard any shells that stay shut.

steps.title: Serve
steps.body: Remove the bay leaves, scatter with parsley, and ladle into wide bowls with the toast and a bowl for shells.

coverage_contribution: Mussels, clams, and shrimp each appear alone in the catalog; there is no mixed-seafood stew and no Californian seafood dinner. A shellfish feast that is still a one-pot meal.
near_duplicate_review: Compared with garlic-tomato-mussels: four kinds of seafood in a fennel-tomato-wine stew, not mussels alone in garlic tomato broth. Compared with linguine-with-clams: a brothy stew with bread, not clams with pasta. Compared with brazilian-fish-moqueca: tomato and white wine with fennel, not coconut milk, peppers, and dende oil.
not_duplicate_of: Not bouillabaisse (no saffron, rouille, or fish stock) and not zuppa di pesce over pasta.
